title: 2013 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: Squares \(ABCD,\) \(EFGH,\) and \(GHIJ\) are equal in area. Points \(C\) and \(D\) are the midpoints of sides \(IH\) and \(HE,\) respectively. What is the ratio of the area of the shaded pentagon \(AJICB\) to the sum of the areas of the three squares?

solutions.text:
Let each square have side length \(1\), so the total area of the three squares is \(3\). It is easier to subtract the unshaded region to the left of diagonal \(AJ\) from this total.

Using the solution diagram, rectangle \(EDKF\) has area \(1\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac12\), and triangle \(AKJ\) has area \[\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac32\cdot2=\dfrac32.\] Thus the unshaded area is \(\dfrac12+\dfrac32=2\), so the shaded pentagon has area \(3-2=1\).

The requested ratio is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\).

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Let each square have side length \(1\).
Subtract the unshaded rectangle and triangle from the total area \(3\).
